question: On 12 May 2021, in Written Question P-002551/20211, the Commission was asked, for the second time (following Written Question E-5452/20202), what action it would take to force Germany to adapt its decision of 14 June 2018 on the conversion of the European Baccalaureate and to replace it with a non-discriminatory decision that complies with European law.
The question also asked specifically how the Commission intended to guarantee the rights of 2021 school leavers. The Commission opened an infringement procedure against Germany on 9 June 2021.

In April 2024, the problems caused by the German conversion decision remain unsolved, and are in fact worse: the average Baccalaureate grades of European school graduates, when converted into German grades, have gone down, while German school leavers have benefited from an inflation of grades.

There is therefore an urgent need for the Commission to reinstate discrimination-free access to German universities for European school graduates from 2021 and subsequent years. In this context, I ask the Commission: 1.
What concrete steps has the Commission taken since May 2021 to address the issue of the conversion of European Baccalaureate marks into the German marking scheme?
How has the Commission pursued the infringement procedure and what stage has been reached (letter of formal notice or reasoned opinion)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.7.2024) The Commission initiated an infringement procedure on the matter of the conversion of Baccalaureate grades of European school graduates against Germany in June 2021. This took place before the first European Baccalaureate graduates received their results under the new marking system.

The Commission is keeping the infringement procedure open, monitoring the practical application of the German conversion system under the new marking system. With the new facts at our disposal, the Commission continues exchanges with the German authorities. Depending on their evolution, the Commission will decide on the next steps to follow.
